audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer read 'Skill' on six of seven rows while the content layer read Annie/Annie/Annie/Annie/Annie/Fizz/Fizz. Row 5 was worse: full said Fizz, content said Annie, and the content layer's own whys[4] said 'Level 6 favors Fizz'.
audit.why: Annie owns levels 1-3, when Urchin Strike reaches only 550 and Playful/Trickster is not yet learned or sits on 16s. Level 6 goes to Fizz: Chum the Waters sticks from 1300 range and the knockup guarantees his combo, while his hop already answers her point-and-click stun.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Annie/Annie/Annie/Annie/Fizz/Fizz/Fizz across both layers as one atomic group; win[4] flipped to match the full side and the whys text that were already there.
sources: currentText full phases[4].side and content whys[4]

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4], spikes[1] and mid all credit Playful/Trickster to level 6 and call it 'his ultimate' ('Level 6 favors Fizz: his ultimate grants an untargetable dash-stomp combo').
audit.why: Playful/Trickster is his E — available from level 3, 16/14/12/10/8s. His ultimate is Chum the Waters: 120/100/80s, 1300 range, attaches a fish, slows, then knocks up. So the untargetable hop is an early-lane fact, and level 6 adds guaranteed engage, not mobility.
audit.corrected: Hop moved back to level 3 with its cooldown; level 6 rewritten around Chum the Waters.
sources: enemyKit E and R text and cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: The page said the hop 'dodges your whole combo' without saying why that matters more here than elsewhere, and it never mentioned the Seastone Trident auto-reset. Two smaller errors: spikes[2] and wants.you[2] tell you to avoid walls he can 'hop off of'.
audit.why: Annie's stun is delivered by a point-and-click Q, so untargetability is a total answer to it — bait-and-count is the only counterplay, and that is the matchup. missingInteractions flags the auto-reset: Seastone Trident empowers his next attack, so the wind-up, not Urchin Strike, is the cue. Playful/Trickster requires no terrain — Fizz vaults on his own spear anywhere. What actually beats standing behind minions is Urchin Strike dashing THROUGH a target to reach you.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and dosFull[1].d rebuilt; the wall claim replaced with the minion-dash truth in spikes[2], mid and wants.you[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: Every reference to the hop's cooldown was the word 'real' — no number anywhere.
audit.why: 16s at rank 1 falling to 8s at rank 5 is the difference between a lane you can trade in and one you cannot.
audit.corrected: Both ends of the range stated, and the late-game text keyed to the 8-second version.

edits.before: - Fizz Playful / Trickster: matchup-defining — The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E Molten Shield like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.

edits.before: If Fizz takes first blood, tighten up: Playful / Trickster is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with Q refunds and stay relevant through stocked-stun threat.
edits.after: If Fizz takes first blood, stop saving the stun for a duel he can hop out of — spend it on his arrival instead. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn't: farm with Q refunds and stay relevant through stocked-stun threat.

edits.before: Carry through the one button — Flash-Tibbers on two is a won fight; your whole game is engineering the radius.
edits.after: Carry the one button — Flash-Tibbers him the moment the hop lands, while he is committed and out of dodges.

edits.after: Ahead, shrink the lane: hold the glow, deny CS while his hop sits on 16s, and Flash-Tibbers the recovery attempt — fed Annie ends games at 20.

edits.after: Fizz spends Playful / Trickster early — that is a 16-second window where he cannot dodge.

edits.before: First item favors Fizz: E-dodge into R-stomp gives him reliable burst that punishes Annie near walls or minions.
edits.after: First item favors Fizz: the hop dodges her stun and Chum the Waters re-opens the burst she has no second answer to.

edits.before: 2+ items favor Fizz: his mobility lets him dive, burst, and escape even through a stun, outscaling Annie's flatter combo.
edits.after: 2+ items favor Fizz: an 8-second untargetable hop lets him dive, burst and leave, outscaling Annie's flatter combo.

edits.before: Fizz's Seastone Trident poke is short-range and his E dodge is on a real cooldown, so Annie's stun punishes any dive attempt before his kit fully comes online.
edits.after: Urchin Strike only reaches 550 and Playful/Trickster is 16s at rank 1, so Annie's stun punishes every dive attempt during the window where his hop is down.

edits.before: Playful/Trickster finally gives Fizz an untargetable dash-stomp combo that closes the early gap and threatens a real burst kill.
edits.after: Chum the Waters is the level-6 spike: a 1300-range fish that sticks, slows, then knocks up — the hop had been his since level 3.

edits.before: With one item Fizz can combo E-dodge into R-stomp for reliable burst that punishes Annie for standing near minions or walls.
edits.after: With one item, Fizz dashes clean through a minion with Urchin Strike to reach you — standing behind the wave is no protection at all.

edits.before: A scaled Fizz becomes a slippery backline diver who's hard to lock down even with a landed stun, outscaling Annie's flatter burst combo.
edits.after: A scaled Fizz goes untargetable every 8 seconds, so even a landed stun buys you one short window rather than a kill on him.

edits.before: Level 6 is his turning point: Playful/Trickster grants an untargetable stomp combo that finally gives him a reliable engage and burst tool, closing the gap you built earlier. Respect his all-in range once he hits 6, especially near terrain he can hop off of, and keep your own stun ready to answer his dive. If you're ahead from early lane dominance, keep playing for poke rather than close-range trades where his combo shines.
edits.after: Level 6 is his turning point: Chum the Waters throws a fish 1300 units that sticks, slows and knocks you up, guaranteeing the combo the hop used to gamble on. Respect his all-in range once he hits 6 — Playful/Trickster needs no terrain, it works anywhere — and keep your stun for his arrival rather than his approach. If you're ahead from early lane, play poke over close trades where his combo shines.

edits.before: A fully scaled Fizz is a genuine backline assassin who can hop in, burst, and hop back out even through a landed stun, making him hard to fully punish in extended fights. Annie's Tibbers-stun combo is still a real answer if you land it first, but Fizz's mobility means he often dictates when the fight happens. Ward chokepoints and walls, and try to force fights on your terms before he gets a second item online.
edits.after: A fully scaled Fizz is a genuine backline assassin who hops in untargetable, bursts, and hops back out through a landed stun, so he is hard to punish in any extended fight. Annie's Tibbers-stun is still a real answer when it lands on his arrival, but Fizz picks when the fight happens. Ward the chokepoints and force fights on your terms before his second item lands.

edits.before: Avoid grouping near walls he can hop off of
edits.after: Avoid standing behind minions he can dash through
